message.content: The lion (Panthera leo) and the zebra (Equus quagga) diverged from a common ancestor that lived in the **Laurasiatherian** clade during the **Eocene epoch** (about 56–34 million years ago). This ancestor was a small, generalized mammal that gave rise to the separate lineages that eventually became the modern carnivores (lion) and perissodactyls (zebra).
